version.note: High Fidelity, September 1979, p. 129 explicitly identifies Craft’s Columbia MS 6216 as the first version, distinguishing it from the 1928 revision in his separate complete-Webern set. The original score heads movement IV Langsam, marcia funebre; its central solo begins on alto flute, not the revision’s clarinet. Section landmarks are broad score-proportion timings, without aural review.

performers.note: The original labels and contemporary review name the orchestra and conductor. The fourth piece uses wind instruments and percussion; individual players are not identified.

date.note: The sources establish the commercial issue but do not state this track’s recording-session date. It is not assigned a date from Craft’s separate 1950s complete-Webern project.

place.note: No recording venue is stated in the transfer metadata or original labels.

catalogue.note: Internet Archive dates this US stereo LP to 1960. Audio magazine reviewed MS 6216 in August 1961 and separately identified mono ML 5616. The rights assessment uses the conservative publication bound of 1961.

matrixTakeSides.note: The label lists Schoenberg as band 1 and Webern’s six pieces as bands 2–7; No. 4 is therefore band 5. The matrix is printed on the label. No session take or stamper suffix is asserted.

credits.note: The transfer institution is identified; no personal mastering credit is inferred from an operator account.

composition.value: Underlying Webern composition is out of copyright under ordinary life-plus-70 terms.
composition.note: Webern died in 1945. The original version was first published in 1913. This assessment concerns the composition in life-plus-70 territories, not every edition or jurisdiction; copyright in the cited 1961 score edition is separate and no worldwide clearance is asserted for that printed score.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis: commercial publication no later than 1961, before 1963.
recording.note: Audio’s August 1961 review establishes commercial availability of the exact LP. The Archive’s 1960 date may identify an earlier issue; the conservative 1961 bound is sufficient for the project’s former 50-year phonogram-term rule. This is not a Creative Commons licence; US recording status is not established.
